1: This presentation brings together the substantive tests and mechanism audits discussed in the chat. The corrected shared S3 method supplies the primary numerical baseline. The sequence distinguishes evolved trajectories, identical-state frozen-flow controls, local budget reconstructions, and earlier calculations with a known reference-force mismatch. The outputs identify mechanisms in the implemented model. They do not establish a physically converged speed of invasion into initially dry ice.
2: The main test families are the porosity-wave benchmark, the two Europa permeability trajectories, a flat-layer and centered-body geometry comparison, and 100-year warm and cold centered-body runs. The remaining slides explain dry-cell wetting, dilation, the controlled kc comparison, and conduction. The appendix retains the earlier boundary checks, pressure-reference audit, reproducibility and regularization results, and interrupted setup tests. No Titan trajectory was generated or verified in this sequence.
3: The shared numerical block evaluates buoyancy, solves coupled Stokes and Darcy flow, computes pressure-head-driven relative flux, advances enthalpy by advection and conduction, and recovers temperature and liquid fraction. The wave keeps its original exponent 2 and nonzero background porosity. Europa and centered cases use exponent 3. The shared head correction is fsVec = fsVec + (Pi_5 + Ra). The Darcy calculation uses the same sealed face mobility and solved pressure head as the enthalpy calculation. The actual-conductivity timestep flag remains enabled. An impermeable wall constrains normal flux while boundary enthalpy and liquid fraction evolve. Europa has a fixed cold surface and a sealed outer base at z=-2 km. Its delivery plane z=0 is internal. The Cartesian boxes are closed and insulated on every side.
4: The corrected long porosity-wave run completed 800 simulated years in 2,464 updates. Its 256 x 1024 Cartesian grid uses the supplied CSV wave, background phi=0.001, and kc=5.6e-11 m2. The displayed comparison is a saved snapshot at 575.462353 years and step 1772. The numerical peak speed is 7.15162087 m/year versus theoretical 7.1946405 m/year, a difference of -0.59794%. The recorded amplitude change is -0.699878%. The analytic reference translates the supplied initial wave using an interpolant for the reference only. No numerical snapshot is synthesized. The bounded, nonzero-background benchmark supports the solver method but does not validate invasion of exactly dry ice.

6: Both Europa trajectories use the same corrected archived solver and impact initial state, cylindrical geometry, material laws, cubic permeability law, and closed external base. Only kc differs. The lower region z<0 starts at phi=0 and 273 K. Delivery means cumulative net downward liquid transfer across z=0. The plotted milestone is delivery of 50% of the initial shell melt, reached at actual diagnostic times 82.5246904 years for high kc and 623.5251 years for low kc. No milestone time is interpolated. The low-kc time is about 7.56 times longer. Pressure and matrix motion adjust in the coupled system, so a factor 1e8 in mobility does not produce a factor 1e8 in delivery speed.

It does not require every shell cell to reach phirem. Initial shell liquid is 31.7803512837 km3. 10: For source-free incompressible phases, the mixture constraint is div(v_s+q)=0. Solid mass conservation gives D_s(phi)/Dt=(1-phi) div(v_s) when phase change is negligible. Positive solid divergence can increase porosity within an already wet region. The selected initial Europa cell at r=1.7 km and z=8.15 km starts at phi=0.4375. Its high-kc divergence is 19.1262559/year, with dilation porosity rate 10.7585189/year. Low kc gives divergence 3.34355098e-7/year and dilation rate 1.88074743e-7/year. Actual adaptive timesteps differ slightly. Dilation accounts for 88.915% of the local high-kc Eulerian phi increase in this deliberately selected example. That is not a fraction of total delivery or migration. Flux convergence and dilation are linked by the constraint, so their co-location is not independent causal proof.
11: The controlled audit solves four frozen flows. Within each pair, H, phi, T, geometry, rheology, gravity, and external walls are identical. Only kc changes, and pressure and velocity are recomputed. The later pair both use the high-kc one-year shape. The low-kc control is not a low-kc trajectory evolved to one year. Across z=4 km at that shape, high-kc carried flow is -17.941467079, Darcy flow +21.887463382, and net flow +3.945996303 million m3/year/m. Low kc gives +0.406986862, +0.000000351411, and +0.406987213. Downward is positive. The net ratio is 9.695627. Initially the carried rates differ by only 0.125%, and the selected high-kc dry-face solid speed is slightly smaller. The speed-up arises as relative segregation and coupled matrix flow reorganize, rather than from a simple multiplication of the initial bulk velocity.
12: The corrected geometry test uses Cartesian x=0-20 km and z=-2 to10 km, 100 x120 cells, closed and insulated walls, 273 K initially, kc=1.85e-8 m2, and exponent 3. The flat case contains water across the full width above z=4 km and has no imposed lateral perturbation. It remains nearly hydrostatic through 8.893483 years, with max absolute phi change 1.240337e-9. The centered case restricts the initial water to x=5-15 km above z=4 km, introducing lateral density structure and circulation. The flat case starts with twice the water volume, 120 versus 60 million m3/m. This is therefore a geometry demonstration rather than a volume-controlled comparison. A perfectly symmetric equilibrium staying still does not establish stability to lateral perturbations.

18: The cold lower-half cumulative energy gain is 1.5245154661948372e16 J/m. Net advected enthalpy supplies 1.524291761185562e16 J/m and net conductive input supplies 2.237050092879082e12 J/m. The conductive fraction is 0.0146738432% of net regional heat gain. Conduction between liquid and neighboring ice within that fixed region cancels in its regional net total. The map records both positive and negative time-integrated conductive energy increments in fixed cells. Whole-domain conductive gain is numerically zero, consistent with insulated external walls. Positive cumulative cell contributions sum to 5.06815e12 J/m and negative contributions sum to its opposite. The small regional percentage therefore cannot be interpreted as zero local effect or a causal percentage of migration.

This event is not evidence of spontaneous pore nucleation in intact stationary ice.
20: The supported description is permeability-enhanced liquid segregation coupled to viscous compaction and dilation within already wet material. Checked dry-to-wet grid-cell events begin with material motion and enthalpy transport. The model recovers phi as liquid volume fraction from enthalpy. It does not evolve a separate empty-pore, fracture-damage or cavitation field. At an exactly dry harmonic face, both permeability and q are zero. When all incident q vanish, the mixture constraint sets solid divergence approximately to zero while still allowing nonzero solid translation and circulation. Once neighboring cells contain liquid, their relative-flow path becomes active. Porosity modifies permeability through phi cubed and modifies the retained melt-softening rheology. The evidence does not establish a converged physical invasion speed or dry-pore nucleation mechanism.
